正午，天怎么突然黑了？: At noon, why did the sky suddenly go dark?
抬头看：不是云，是月亮正好走到太阳前面。城市路灯自己亮了起来。站在那一小块本影里: Look up: not clouds—the Moon has stepped in front of the Sun. Streetlights come on by themselves. Only people standing inside that small umbra see this.
这根影子，是月亮的: This shadow belongs to the Moon
拉远看清全貌：最左边是太阳（距离压缩了两百多倍才画得进来），光线笔直向右。月亮挡: Zoom out for the whole picture: at the far left is the Sun (pulled more than two hundred times closer so it fits in the frame), its light travelling straight to the right. The Moon stands in the way and trails a thin shadow cone 58 Earth radii long whose tip just touches Earth.
差四万公里，就只剩金环: Forty thousand kilometres short, and only a golden ring remains
月亮的轨道是椭的。这回它离地球远了四万多公里，影锥够不到地面——月面盖不满日面，: The Moon’s orbit is elliptical. This time it is more than forty thousand kilometres farther from Earth, so the shadow cone cannot reach the ground—the lunar disc cannot cover the Sun and leaves a golden ring. Magnify that ring: the Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon and, by coincidence, about 400 times farther away; totality and annularity differ by just this distance.
所以不是每个月都有: Which is why not every month has one
月亮轨道歪了 5.1°，大约是日月视直径的十倍。贴着黄道面看：大多数新月从太阳上: The Moon’s orbit is tilted by 5.1°, about ten times the apparent size of the Sun or Moon. Watching edge-on: at most new moons the Moon passes above or below the Sun, and the shadow cone misses Earth. A solar eclipse can only happen when new moon is near one of the two doorways—the ascending or descending node. There are only two such eclipse seasons each year.
这回，轮到地球的影子: This time, it is Earth’s shadow
半个月后，月亮绕到地球背后，钻进地球的影子里。它没有变黑，而是泛起铜红：地球大气: Half a month later, the Moon swings behind Earth and dives into Earth’s shadow. It does not go black; it glows copper-red, because Earth’s atmosphere bends the red light of every sunrise and sunset on the planet into the umbra. Earth’s shadow is two and a half lunar diameters wide out at the Moon, so a total lunar eclipse can be watched for more than an hour.
本世界模拟，不是观测录像: A simulation from this world, not observational footage
从天上，你看不见日食: From orbit, you do not see the eclipse
卫星只看见影子扫过地球。中央金边深核是本影——站在那里看见日全食；周围品红圈是半: A satellite only sees the shadow sweep across Earth. The gold-rimmed dark core is the umbra—stand there and you see a total solar eclipse; the magenta ring around it is the penumbra, where it is only partial.
